We will do our utmost, Mr. Seselj, to make sure that your voice is being heard, that we have heard what you had to say, and that the Prosecution can be heard also. And to conclude, the Trial Chamber is able to draw its own conclusions at the end of all those hearings which will take place in the future. I wish you a nice evening, and as you know we shall meet again tomorrow morning at 9.00. Mrs. Dahl.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I wanted to just bring up -- there's a couple of outstanding motions that I would request the Chamber's attention to. We're still waiting for the approval of the second amended indictment. I need to file updated schedules. We've looked at the schedules that were prepared in 2003 and connected them with the evidence that's been disclosed, we want to correct misspellings and dates of birth and make sure that all of the names that are disclosed are properly reflected. There's also a motion for adjudicated facts. The motion was filed in 2006, it's been fully briefed and translated and it's at issue. It would help us to have an early ruling on that motion so that we know what facts we will be able to rely on as accepted as adjudicated by the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. That's not a problem. The Trial Chamber will hand down these decisions. We need time to confer over these matters, but you can rely on us. We will hand down these decisions as soon as possible. Mr. Seselj, as the Prosecution wish to take the floor, you may take the floor also.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to inform you, Judges, that the Prosecution systematically called all my potential witnesses who had given statements to my legal associates, and these statements are attached in my criminal report and the attachment to my criminal report. Some of them refused to be interviewed by the OTP and some were brought to The Hague as a matter of fact and then they refused to be Prosecution witnesses here and they said that they would be my witnesses. Just like I am forbidden to contact the witnesses of the Prosecution whose names I know, the Prosecutor is even more prohibited to contact potential Defence witnesses, people she knows are potential Defence witnesses in advance. They are exerting impermissible pressure against Defence witnesses. I'm going to give you a name.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... sorry, Your Honour, we need to go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- The Prosecution heard him earlier on but he refused to testify for them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... one moment. Yes, this might be the name of a protected witness, if so we'll have to have a redacting order.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He's not protected? I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's not a single protected Defence witness. He is a Defence witness --

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- not a single Defence witness is asking for protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, from what Mr. Seselj says, he's a Defence witness, the one he gave the name of.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj doesn't know who all of our witnesses are, and we've discussed this before. The naming of names and the redaction or going into closed session needs to be neutral, otherwise the act of redaction discloses, in fact, whether or not it's a protected witness. So we really need to respect that, otherwise I will be jumping up like a jack-in-the-box that Mr. Seselj called me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Last time, Mr. Seselj, I told you whenever you want to state a name, it might be the name of a Prosecution witness, then you have to say Mr. X or you ask to move to private session to speak about it; otherwise, I'll have to issue an order to redact the name. I know that you said that in your flight, but you raise a true problem not provided for by the Rules --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a violation of the Rules, Judge. This is a violation of the Rules. Not a single Defence witness is a protected witness. I don't dare mention a single name in public sessions. Why should I defend myself at all then? As I hear some Prosecution witnesses here, I'm going to mention different names of people who participated in events. The Prosecutor cannot ask for closed session all the time because it's possible that I'm going to mention a protected Prosecution witness. What would that be like if I mention a name of a person as a participant in a particular event, I'm mentioning that name regardless of whether this is a potentially protected witness or not, I'm referring to someone as a participant in an event. There are people who are participants in the joint criminal enterprise according to the Prosecutor, so then I do not dare mention any of their names either because some of them appeared as protected witnesses in some other case? That really makes no sense. I can mention any name unless I was informed beforehand that such and such a person is a protected witness. In that case, I observe measures of protection. I never disclosed a name of a person who I was told was a Defence -- who was a Prosecution witness who is protected. What do you mean that I cannot mention a single name? How is that possible?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: I can't hear the translation because of the volume of Mr. Seselj's voice, because he be please requested to lower the volume.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Ms. Dahl, when Mr. Oberschall comes to testify, it might be that during the cross-examination Mr. Seselj might be -- might have to give names. He's not at all aware of who is protected among the witnesses, you see, so it may be that he might state names. So what is your view on this?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: I think that that presents a different context, and what the argument that Mr. Seselj is doing is taking the rule and trying to show its application in a different context. If we're talking about individuals in a factual context or in questioning, that's completely different and presents a different problem than Mr. Seselj saying that one person is a witness or another person is a witness. And I don't think that cross-examination of Dr. Oberschall is going to raise the same issues regarding the privacy of witnesses. It's when somebody is identified as a witness in this case as opposed to a percipient witness that the expert might be talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Dahl, I don't know what Mr. Seselj is going to say, I don't know at all, but let us imagine that in his opening statement Mr. Seselj is -- said that he was going to speak about the pre-trial brief. I'm just giving an example because I'm not in his head, but after all I'm used to -- I've been used to criminal trials for 30 years, so I can pre-empt or have an idea what's going to happen just as well. He could say the Prosecutor in paragraph 4 of page 24 says this and this. I challenge what is said there and I'm going to demonstrate through witnesses X, Y, Z, Mr. This and Madam This, that this is wrong or false. And he's going to come up with names. As far as I can see, he is allowed to give those names because that's his case. I don't know what my fellow Judges feel, but you can't just get on your feet and ask for a redaction, all the more so if we are talking about or if he mentions four individuals who he has already contacted and said they were going to be his Defence witnesses. So that's it. So far we've had this problem on a couple of occasions, but on Wednesday he's free to talk, and unlike what he said, nobody's going to cut him off and he can express himself.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: The pre-trial brief has two forms: One is a public brief that includes references to witnesses according to a pseudonym. There's a confidential brief that discloses more information. I don't think it's appropriate to jeopardize the safety and security of witnesses to name names in an opening statement. I will not be naming names in mine because our sensitive witnesses deserve the privacy and protection. Mr. Seselj's naming names as well presents a privacy issue for those individuals. They may have security and privacy issues that they should have the opportunity to bring before the Chamber coincident with their appearance here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, Ms. Dahl, I do understand what you say, but you raise a real problem there. Mr. Seselj in his opening statement is going to present his case. He said so. There are witnesses whose identities he doesn't know because that's the very subject of his claims and his grievances. Therefore, when he speaks on Wednesday, he can say: Well, what is written here is wrong, is false, because I've got people who are going to say the opposite. And if then were to name names, I can't see why he should be prevented from naming names. Or what could prevent him because per se he doesn't know if those people are protected witnesses or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: I'm not clear on the procedure, because Mr. Seselj told us at one of the Status Conferences that he was going to reserve his opening statement until the commencement of the Defence case. If that's so, by then he will know all of our witnesses because they will have testified presumably and they would have been disclosed. If he is giving an opening statement tomorrow, that's a new problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's not play on words, Ms. Dahl. For four years I've been sitting just about every day in a courtroom. So if anyone knows the procedure, I am the one, and I am telling you that in his opening statement which is a presentation of his Defence system, he is entitled to address any subject that is of interest because he's the accused; you're not. So if he's the accused, if he wants to try and defeat your case, your strategy, he can do so by saying, Well, the Prosecutor in paragraph 4 said this, I have Mr. So-and-so and Mr. So-and-so who's going to testify to say the opposite. Or Mr. X wrote a book -- after all, you're not going to forbid him from saying so. I mean, I don't know what my fellow Judges feel about it, we're going to discuss this of course in time by Wednesday, but I'm expressing my views, and listening to you I'm under the impression that you really want to lock him up, to lock the freedom of expression, and trap the Judges into a role where they would let you go -- I mean let you do whatever pleases you. It is out of the question. I wanted to say this to you. You are right, there are protected witnesses and nobody is supposed to know their identity; you're quite right on that one. And Mr. Seselj also has to comply with this. However, if he doesn't know in advance the fact that certain people might be protected witnesses, I mean he's not going to know about them because when we start -- the time has not started running, so what prevents him from saying M. Durant or Mr. So-and-so is going to say this because he's a Defence witness, and then it will turn out that this M. Durant will be your witness that could happen. I don't know, but that's the problem. Listen, we're going to break.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I very briefly, Judge, very briefly, please. On Thursday I'm providing a witness statement under Rule 84 bis, and you allowed me to speak for four hours. That is a statement by the accused, whereas my opening statement will be when the Defence case starts. And second, very briefly, I never got the confidential version of the pre-trial brief. I just have the public version, and the witnesses are under pseudonyms. Even if I wanted to, I cannot disclose a single name that has not been disclosed to me. This is the public version, it is on the internet, the one that I received. So what Mrs. Dahl is saying makes no sense at all. And if I am speaking about participants in events about which I do not know that they may be potential protected witnesses, I will not know it, I will not be aware of it, and nobody else will be aware of it. If tomorrow morning they let me to have a list of all the protected witnesses, I will not mention those names, then. And they are duty-bound on Rule 69 to give me that list tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Dahl, Mr. Seselj tells you what the solution. If you have any concern regarding a witness, just -- just say as early as tomorrow these are the witnesses of concern, and Mr. Seselj, as he's just said, will not be allowed to name names. And then your worries or concerned may be assuaged.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: He has not provided us with a list of his witnesses. I want to prevent him from hurting people. I do not want him to be able to thrust people unwillingly into the public eye. He has admitted lying and making up things in order to suit his own purposes. I do not want that to happen this week where there is an enormous amount of public interest in the opening of the case. I don't have his witness list, so I can't go through and try to figure out if there's some overlap where I need to be cautious, and anybody he mentions has a privacy interest. We went through this when he had one of his associates out putting out signs to create public support for Ratko Mladic. This is a very serious matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't want to go into that. Rule 84 bis provides that the accused, after what you say, after your opening statement, can appear. 84 bis does not say that his testimony must take into account the issue of protected witnesses that he doesn't know of; you are the one who adds this. Therefore, tomorrow -- on Wednesday, if he is to speak, to say that in order to support his Defence he's of the view that Mrs. Y, Mr. X are individuals who are going to come and support his version of the facts and if it so happens that these people also were your witnesses, I don't even know what he's going to say. I don't even know what he's going to say, and you are already sort of going ahead. But if he's going to name a name, I'm not going to check straight away to make sure that that name is the name of somebody's who protected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must say something. If the accused does not plan to make an opening statement the day after tomorrow but only a statement that he is authorised to make the day after tomorrow, we can indeed ask him to make sure that he does not use or resort to names during that statement, to try and avoid naming names. He can do so. He can use names when the time comes for him to make an opening statement for his Defence, for his case I believe. He could indeed, be courteous enough for us to be able to progress, to make headway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, my fellow Judge just said something. What do you think?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that is simply impossible. Tomorrow at least I have to mention Jacques Chirac and what Jacques Chirac stated to the Serbian people, and statements by a whole series of other Western statesmen. It's not impossible for me to refrain from mentioning any names. I have to mention the key people from the General Staff who took part in the war, generals who commanded the army, chiefs of military security services. I have to mention the names of the participants in the JCE who are mentioned in the indictment, who are mentioned in the Milosevic indictment but not in mine, in the Krajisnik indictment, but not in mine. All this gibberish, and I have tell you this: Ms. Christine Dahl is lying through her teeth when she says here in the courtroom that I admitted to lying. I never admitted to lying anywhere because I never lied in the first place, not in my testimony in the Milosevic trial, not in my previous statements. I just explained the nature of certain statements, and she is lying shamelessly that I admitted to lying before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, you mention well-known names, you intend to name them, that's fine. But the problem is not there. The problem arises if you name the names of victims of people who were there in the field, that's the problem. If you mention the head of the intelligence service, that's fine, they're all known names. The problem is really at the level of the area. Are you going to mention names from the field or not?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Never. I will never mention a single victim's name unless that name is mentioned in the public version of the pre-trial brief, and I can mention the names of commanders of volunteer units. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is now 7.30.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Names of my prominent volunteers, people I trusted.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, very briefly, I am in agreement with Judge Lattanzi's observation regarding the purposes of Rule 84 bis. It's not an opening statement. It's not necessary at this point for Mr. Seselj to declare all of the people whom he thinks will support his case. We cannot give him a list of witnesses in order to tell him whom to steer away from, and I can only think that the Rule 84 bis statement of the accused has to do about his acts and conduct not, generally speaking, his theory of Defence or the number of people who support his view of the facts. And I would ask that we keep the focus on preventing further harm and protect the privacy of the people. There won't be this issue once we get his list of witnesses. Their needs can be addressed by the Victims and Witnesses Unit, and by the time that Mr. Seselj makes his opening statement and declares his defence and what he thinks the evidence will prove, we will have disclosed all of our witnesses and they will have testified, so that issue won't present itself in the same context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mention Rule 84 bis, but there's also Rule 84 prior to the opening statement by the Prosecutor. Each party, you and him, can make an opening statement. So he is entitled to make an opening statement. However, the Defence, him, therefore, can decide to make an opening statement after the presentation of the Prosecution case and before the Defence presents their case. So it is up to him to decide. If he wants to speak on Wednesday, he does so; if he wishes to speak after you have presented your case, he can do so. Therefore, there is total equality. The Prosecutor will present their case, he makes his opening statement, you make yours, and the Rules say that he's also free to make a similar opening statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm very sorry, I just wanted to say that Mr. Seselj himself said that he can -- he has decided to present his opening statement at the beginning of his Defence case. Therefore, that's what I understood and the day after tomorrow, on that day he's going to limit himself to a statement that he was authorised to make, but it is not his opening statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you enlighten us, on Wednesday, what do you plan to do? On what basis are you going to speak?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your colleague, Ms. Lattanzi, is completely right. I am making a statement of the accused under Rule 84, that's what I told you also at the Status Conference when you allowed me four hours for that statement. That's a statement of the accused. The Rules of Procedure and Evidence envisaged the privilege for the accused vis-a-vis the Prosecution. The Prosecution can make an opening statement only once, whereas I am entitled both to a statement of the accused and the opening statement. On Thursday, under Rule 84 bis, I'm making a statement of the accused. I repeated that at several Status Conferences. The previous Trial Chamber gave me two and a half hours, giving three hours to the Prosecution; you increased that to four hours for me and four hours for the Prosecution, and I believe that is quite appropriate. I am making a statement of the accused. I am going to be presenting my views on the indictment and the pre-trial brief of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Now, the time has come to finish. My apologies to the interpreters, but we had to look into this. We shall convene again tomorrow at 9.00. Thank you.
